terms.comment: Morgan–Owens argues that cinēmatographēum ought to mean a film studio (M-O s.v. movie theater).
Traupman and Andresian both mark the first vowel long, as in Greek κῑνέω, κῑ́νημα, and Traupman writes cīnēmatēum too (52, 348); the other forms here are written with a short i.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. movie theater, cinema.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 52.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 52, 348, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
